prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a hit while turning left. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1359; do not mention it.)
text:
Our firm represents the claimant in connection with the collision that occurred while our client was making a left turn. The impact caused our client significant injuries, and we expect the matter to involve a claim for medical expenses, lost income, and pain and suffering.

Please direct all further communication regarding this claim to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person. If your insured or any representative of the company wishes to discuss the incident, they should do so only through this firm.

We request that you disclose the bodily injury and property damage liability limits of every policy that may apply to this loss, including any excess or umbrella coverage, and confirm the identity of the adjuster assigned to the file.

Finally, we ask that your company preserve all evidence relating to this incident. This includes photographs, dash camera or telematics data, recorded statements, claim notes, repair estimates, vehicle inspection reports, and any electronic communications. Please treat this letter as formal notice of our client's claim and of the obligation to retain all related materials.
